notes: v1.14.567 — THE ASSISTANT COMES BACK: THE FAKE LOCK THAT WAS BREAKING IT IS GONE. PUNCHLIST P-1. One visible change: PHANTOM_PROXY_KEY and the x-phantom-key header are deleted, so phantomAPI now sends Content-Type only. ⛔ THE HEADER WAS THE DEFECT, NOT A PROTECTION. The Worker never read the token — its origin check replaced token auth — and its CORS allows the Content-Type request header ONLY, so a non-listed header made Safari send a preflight the Worker would not clear and the POST never left the phone. ⭐ DIAGNOSED BY THE ERROR STRING, NOT BY ASSUMPTION: the punchlist recorded 'API 400', which can ONLY come from vaAsk:50964's !resp.ok branch and therefore requires a real HTTP response — impossible if the preflight is blocked, because fetch REJECTS instead. The owner re-read the card on device: it says 'Load failed', which is Safari's CORS message. That single string resolved the contradiction and confirmed the preflight is blocked. ⛔ THE CLIENT HALF SHIPPED AND THE SERVER HALF NEVER DID: .199's own note says the key is inert until the owner pastes the grace-mode Worker and later flips ENFORCE_KEY. That Worker never landed, so the key was inert-by-accident for 368 versions and then turned load-bearing in the wrong direction when the Worker's CORS tightened. ⭐ A TWO-LINE CONTRADICTION IS ALSO CLOSED: the comment immediately above the constant read 'No token is sent from the client' while the next line defined the token and sent it. That line is true again. ⚠ THE PUNCHLIST'S OTHER HALF IS MOOT AND IS NOT DONE: it asked that the real response body be surfaced instead of 'API 400'. There is no 400 — the response never arrives to have a body. Adding 400 to phantomAPI's classifier is worth its own ship but would be unverifiable today, so it is reported rather than smuggled in. ⚠ A SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND WHILE TRACING, REPORTED NOT FIXED: phantomAPI's network-error retry at :18305 gates on err.message.indexOf('fetch'), but Safari's message is 'Load failed' and Chrome's is 'Failed to fetch' — so the retry has never fired on iOS, the target platform, for the life of the app. That is a behaviour change and needs its own ship and its own device verify.
